NOVEMBER 4, 2026  
Paul Bunyan Room, First Floor of City Hall, 73 Harlow Street 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Commissioners Present: Nina Earley, Sundance Campbell, Kelly Chenot, Kal Elmore, Rosemary Lausier, 
Benjamin James, Jennifer Snow 
 
Others: Kayleigh Rienas, Development Assistant 
 
1. A quorum being present the November 4, 2026 meeting of the Commission on Cultural Development 
was called to order by Chair Earley at 5:40 PM. 
 
2. Meeting Minutes – Motion passed to approve the minutes of the June 5 and October 4 meeting.  
 
3.  Committee Reports 
a. ARTober Committee – 
i. Committee Chair Campbell provided an overview of the reflections and feedback 
discussed at the ARTober Committee Meeting. He highlighted the work Commissioner 
James contributed, noting the new branding design and banners. 
b. Cultural Asset – 
i. Committee Chair Elmore noted they are waiting for the Request for Proposal to be 
posted. Chair Earley requested for the Commission to be notified via email when the 
Request for Proposal is live. Earley provided reminders of conflict of interest. The 
Commission discussed the timeline for the Request for Proposal. 
c. Grant Committee – 
i. Committee Chair Snow discussed the Grant Committee Meeting on October 20 to 
evaluate the grant applications, and introduced the applications for review. 
Commissioner Chenot commented that she likes the accessibility outlined by the 
Penobscot Theatre Company. Snow noted that the Robinson Ballet is celebrating their 
50th anniversary. Chair Earley asked whether Some Theatre Company has located a 
new venue – the Commission discussed Some Theatre Company’s circumstance 
surrounding loss of location, assurances outlined in the application, and Commission 
avenues of support. Earley and Chenot expressed appreciating the free and accessible 
components of the Bangor Symphony Orchestra’s application. The Commission 
discussed excitement surrounding increased funds to provide organizations in grants.  
ii. Committee Chair Snow presented the Grant Committee’s recommendations for grant 
awards, including: Penobscot Theatre Company for $5,750.00, Robinson Ballet for 
$5,000, Some Theatre Company for $1,500.00, Bangor Symphony Orchestra for 
$5,750.00, and Bangor Authors’ Collaborative for $2,000. Commissioner Campbell noted 
he must abstain from the vote. Commissioner Snow moved that Campbell shall abstain 
due to conflict of interest. Seconded by Commissioner Chenot. All voting members in 
favor, none opposed. Commissioner Elmore moved that the Commission recommends 
the presented grant split to Council. Seconded by Commissioner Chenot. All voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
4. AI Discussion: 
a. Chair Earley tabled the AI discussion to the next Commission meeting.
5. Remote Policy: 
a. Chair Earley discussed the new remote policy with the Commission. The Commission 
additionally discussed membership renewal, available Commission positions, and attendance 
policies. Commissioner Snow requested a discussion on social media at the upcoming meeting. 
 
6. Adjourned at 6:38 PM.

Memorandum 
To: Commission on Cultural Development 
From: Community & Economic Development Department 
Date: November 24, 2026 
Regarding: Staff Report for December 4, 2026 meeting 
 
Please accept this memorandum as a staff update on a couple of important projects for 
the Commission’s consideration. 
Pickering Square 
To pilot the art display program in Pickering Square, staff recommends displaying artwork on a 
quarterly/seasonal basis. This timeline is encouraged based on staff capacity and the 
Commission’s coinciding Arts & Culture Strategic Plan project. To kickstart the program, please 
consider to following: 
• Formation of a subcommittee 
• Creation of a policy and procedure for filling the spaces – what are the considerations? 
For example:  
o Local relevance – local schools/colleges, local artists, artist in residence/summer 
season artist 
o Public engagement/inclusion – notification of meetings when a decision is made  
o Skill level – does the Commission function as a jury to select based on skill, 
originality or other factors 
• Timelines: 
o When should the dates be for the display cycles? 
o When should submissions be due for each cycle? 
o What is the advertising timeline and strategy to receive submissions? 
o When will the subcommittee meet to select artwork? 
Ultimately, your decision is a recommendation to Council, which will be taken to the Business & 
Economic Development Committee (BED) for final approval. This lead time should be factored 
into your timetable.    
2027 Calendar 
Please see in your packet a drafted 2027 calendar for the Commission’s review. The formation 
of this document intends to serve as a guiding resource for ongoing projects. We would like the 
Commission’s feedback on timelines and deadlines in order for staff to best provide support. 
Additionally, in order to finalize the meeting room schedule at City Hall, we would like to know 
whether you would like the Commission-wide meeting schedule to continue on the alternating 
Wednesday/ Friday basis into 2027.

Issue Date: November 17, 2026 
I.  Introduction 
The City of Bangor and its Commission on Cultural Development requests proposals  from qualified 
consulting firms or individuals to develop a comprehensive Arts & Culture Strategic Plan. This 
strategy will serve as a foundational roadmap to guide the Commission’s future deployment of grant 
funding, public art initiatives, and support for cultural programming. 
 
The final plan will be submitted to the Bangor City Council for formal adoption as an appendix to the 
City's 2022 Comprehensive Plan (this document can be found at www.bangormaine.gov/plans).  
About Bangor and the Project 
The City of Bangor is a vibrant regional center in Maine with a rich history, a strong sense of place, 
and a growing appreciation for the role that arts and culture play in creating a thriving community. 
Located along the Penobscot River, Bangor serves as a regional hub for healthcare, education, 
commerce, entertainment, government, and the arts, welcoming residents and visitors from 
throughout the region. 
With a population of approximately 31,000 residents and a broader regional population of more than 
150,000, Bangor is the cultural and economic center of a large portion of northern, eastern, and 
central Maine. The city is home to a diverse collection of arts and cultural organizations, historic 
resources, creative businesses, festivals, public art, museums, galleries, performing arts venues, 
libraries, and community-based cultural activities. These assets contribute significantly to Bangor's 
identity and quality of life and help distinguish the city as a destination within Maine. 
Bangor is currently experiencing a period of renewed investment and revitalization. Public and 
private investments are bringing new life to historic buildings, strengthening downtown, supporting 
small businesses, improving public spaces, and creating opportunities for residents and visitors to 
live, work, gather, and experience the community.  
The City recognizes that arts and culture are an important component of this revitalization—not 
only because they enrich the lives of residents, but because they contribute to economic 
development, tourism, placemaking, workforce attraction and retention, entrepreneurship, and 
community vitality.

The City also recognizes the importance of ensuring that arts and cultural opportunities are 
accessible and meaningful to all members of the community. Bangor's arts and culture ecosystem 
includes established institutions as well as emerging artists, creative entrepreneurs, neighborhood 
organizations, cultural traditions, and informal community activities. Understanding how these 
individual assets can be better connected, supported, promoted, and leveraged is an important 
opportunity for the City. 
As Bangor looks toward its future, the City seeks to develop a comprehensive Arts and Culture 
Strategy Plan that will establish a clear vision and actionable framework for strengthening the city's 
creative and cultural ecosystem. The strategy should build upon Bangor's existing assets and 
initiatives while identifying opportunities for new partnerships, investment, programming, public 
art, creative economic development, cultural tourism, and community engagement. 
The City is seeking an experienced consultant or consulting team to work collaboratively with 
municipal staff, arts and cultural organizations, artists, businesses, residents, community leaders, 
regional partners, and other stakeholders to develop a strategy that reflects Bangor's unique 
character and aspirations. 
The resulting plan should be practical, forward-looking, and implementable, providing the City and 
its partners with a roadmap for making arts and culture an even more integral part of Bangor's 
economic, community, and downtown development efforts.

IX.  Scope of Services 
A. Cultural Assets Mapping: Execute an updated survey and comprehensive inventory of 
Bangor’s existing cultural, artistic, and historical assets. 
B. Vision Statement: Facilitate a robust public process to define a long-term vision, answering: 
What do we want for the future of arts and culture in Bangor over the next decade? 
C. Strategic Goals: Translate the community vision into concrete, achievable goals, answering: 
What do we need to do to make our vision a reality? 
D. Action Plan: Develop specific, granular action steps and initiatives tied directly to each 
strategic goal. 
E. Funding Strategy: Formulate an efficient, sustainable strategy to fund and resource the 
designated action steps.

F. Partner Identification: Map out the specific individuals, community groups, and organizations 
critical to achieving the plan's goals. 
G. Policy & Regulatory Framework: Evaluate and recommend necessary updates or changes to 
municipal policy, zoning, or city code to support the strategy. 
H. Evaluation & Metrics: Establish a performance measurement framework to track progress and 
adjust strategies as community needs evolve. 
 
X.  Project Management 
The selected consultant will navigate a structured, multi-tiered project management framework 
consisting of: 
A. Project Steering Committee: The consultant will interface primarily with a dedicated project 
Steering Committee. This working group will consist of three (3) members of the Commission 
on Cultural Development, city staff, and four (4) at-large Bangor residents representing key 
organizational stakeholders (e.g. Downtown Bangor Partnership, Bangor Beautiful, Bangor 
Historical Society, or another Bangor arts/cultural stakeholder). 
B. Commission Engagement: The consultant will also work directly with the full Commission on 
Cultural Development during regular or special meetings, where community stakeholders will 
be invited to participate. 
C. Economic Development Alignment: Periodic check-ins with the Bangor Economic Development 
(BED) Committee will be required to ensure alignment with broader city-wide economic goals. 
D. Contract Management:  The Director of Community & Economic Development, or her 
designee, will be the point person for the contract. 
 
XI.  Submission Requirements 
To be considered responsive, proposer must include all requirements in their submission. Failure to 
do so will result in disqualification.  
A. Letter of Interest: A brief introduction outlining the firm or individual’s unique qualifications for 
this specific project. 
B. Firm Qualifications & Experience: Detailed profiles of the firm and key personnel who will be 
assigned to this project, emphasizing experience with municipal cultural planning. 
C. Relevant Project Portfolio: Descriptions of at least three (3) similar projects completed for 
municipalities, including references with current contact information. 
D. Proposed Methodology: A high-level conceptual approach detailing how the firm will execute 
the scope of services, particularly the public outreach and asset mapping components. 
E. Items required in Section VIII above

F. An itemized budget for how the consultant or firm will dedicate resources to the plan.  Included 
in the budget should be an expectation of the services and support from city staff and/or the 
Commission in the creation of the Plan. The budget allotted for this project is $30,000.   
 
XII.  Evaluation and Selection Process 
A selection committee made up of City Staff and the Chair of the Commission on Cultural 
Development will review all responsive submissions. 
• Selection criteria will be based on municipal planning and development experience, strength 
of the proposed public engagement strategy, overall qualifications of the project team, 
methodology, qualification in the arts/culture community, and references. Top candidates 
may be invited to participate in an interview process with the selection committee to present 
and explain their proposal, estimated timeline, and how they will meet Bangor’s need based 
on this RFP prior to award.
